warnings: NASA Table 4-11 values are nominal and not assumed independently verified.
PPT and VAT are distinct technology classes even when colocated in a source table.
ND-15 thrust value is retained as an unresolved unit holdout, not silently normalized.
The Ou et al. efficiency claims differ between abstract and highlights and remain separate.
The two 2026 micro Z-pinch papers are distinct device configurations and must not be pooled.
Lab evidence, flight opportunity, flight demonstrated and operational qualification are separate evidence tiers.
No device ranking is valid until installed mass, DC-bus power, mission service, lifetime and uncertainty boundaries are matched.

NASA Table 4-11 HTML has a [mN] thrust column header for AIS VAT rows while the official PDF text layer has [µN]; manufacturer exact-model pages specify µN values at defined power points. Use manufacturer-reported µN values for source attribution, preserve the NASA HTML unit transcription discrepancy.

AIS manufacturer pages report 40,000 shots, 87 s Isp and 0.13/0.26/0.52 N·s total impulse; main product index additionally reports EOL thrust below 1 µN but does not define EOL test condition. Lifetime, thrust drift, per-shot distribution and failure denominator require independent per-unit validation.

AIS manufacturer product index and detailed product pages disagree on current list prices and lead times; exclude web prices from lifecycle ranking until a dated formal quote and supply configuration are frozen.

AIS DUO/QUAD detailed pages list rep-rate power labels that do not match their advertised power options; retain the raw source values and require manufacturer clarification before rate-based duty-cycle or mission estimates.
AIS PQ/DUO/QUAD source arithmetic implies 3.25 µN·s average total impulse per reported shot per PQ module; this quotient is not a direct impulse-bit measurement or variance.

derived_reference_checks.interpretation: Arithmetic quotient of source-reported total impulse and shot lifetime. It is not a directly measured impulse-bit value or its variance; raw per-shot distributions, failed shots, erosion, plume and end-of-life conditions remain unknown.
